title: 2025-07-02 Redwood POC weekly sync - benchmark review vs baseline provider
summary: Weekly PoC sync to review benchmark runs comparing Redwood POC setup vs your baseline provider. Discussed latency (p50/p95), throughput under concurrency, tail behavior, and tuning knobs (batching, KV cache, quantization). Agreed next steps: share spreadsheet, run customer prompt set, schedule baseline re-run with 8k context, and evaluate private deployment latency implications.
header:
Date: 2025-07-02
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Laura Kim (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (AtlasAI - ML Eng), Carlos Rivera (AtlasAI - VP Eng), Priya Patel (AtlasAI - SRE), Arjun Mehta (AtlasAI - DS)
Recorded: Yes (local recording)
transcript:
[00:00] Laura Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio okay?
[00:06] Maya Singh: Yep, we're good on our side.
[00:10] Laura Kim: Great. This is the weekly PoC sync, main agenda is benchmark review vs your baseline provider, plus tuning recommendations and next steps. Ethan, you want to kick off with the numbers?
[00:18] Ethan Park: Sure, thanks Laura. I sent the spreadsheet earlier, link in the chat, but I'll call out highlights. Test bed: model was redwood-7b-quant-v1 (quantized int8), running on Redwood Dedicated pool (A100 equiv). Baseline provider is the one you currently use, "BaselineCloud" per the sheet, running on their managed endpoint. Workload: generation with 512 tokens target, prompt set of 150 real user prompts from AtlasAI, concurrency sweeps at 1, 4, 8, 16.
[00:40] Carlos Rivera: Quick Q, is the baseline using the exact same model weights, or a similar architecture?
[00:44] Ethan Park: Good call. It's a slightly different checkpoint - same family but not Redwood-verified. We tried to match config (context length, temperature) but there may be minor tokenization differences.
[00:54] Priya Patel: OK, important for fairness but we want to see production-like behavior.
[00:58] Ethan Park: Right. Numbers: at batch size 1 (concurrency 1), p50 latency: Redwood 420ms, BaselineCloud 560ms. p95: Redwood 980ms, BaselineCloud 1.3s. Throughput at steady state (concurrency 8): Redwood 18 requests/sec, BaselineCloud 12 requests/sec. GPU utilization on our side was 72% avg; baseline reported about 85% but with higher variance.
[01:28] Maya Singh: Those p95 deltas look promising. Can you remind us if the 420ms is end-to-end including network?
[01:33] Ethan Park: Yes end-to-end from client to response at our hosted endpoint in us-west-2. One caveat: your baseline endpoints are in us-east-1 which adds ~30-40ms network difference in some runs.
[01:42] Arjun Mehta: Did you run any tests with longer context, like 8k? Our actual prod chats often hit 6-7k.
[01:49] Ethan Park: We did a limited 8k run. There we saw p50 ~1.1s on Redwood vs baseline ~1.45s. Throughput drops predictably; but we also measured KV cache effectiveness for repeated prefixes which reduced p50 to ~700ms for repeated convo slices.
[02:03] Laura Kim: Important note: KV cache behavior depends on session stickiness and routing. For the PoC we used a sticky routing policy to hit the same replica and observe cache hits.
[02:12] Priya Patel: Are there any differences on tokenization that could skew latency? Token length of outputs?
[02:17] Ethan Park: We normalized tokenization in the runner so outputs token count are comparable within ~5% variance.
[02:22] Carlos Rivera: What about tail latency p99? That's what bites us in production.
[02:26] Ethan Park: p99 is higher: Redwood p99 ~2.8s under concurrency 8; BaselineCloud p99 ~4.1s. Some of baseline's p99 spikes coincide with noisy neighbors and autoscaling events on their managed pool.
[02:39] Maya Singh: Noisy neighbors, yep that's been our pain. How deterministic were your runs? Any warm-up effects?
[02:44] Ethan Park: We did 10-minute warm-up and excluded first 2 minutes from metrics. Still some variance across runs but we averaged across three identical sweeps.
[02:53] Laura Kim: I'll call out a few tuning knobs that improved our numbers during the test: continuous batching set to 20ms delay (reduced p50 by ~8% for mid-sized prompts), operator-level kernel selection for attention (saw ~12% perf benefit on 8k), and enabling quantization-specific kernels which helped throughput.
[03:13] Arjun Mehta: On quantization, was there any measurable drop in quality? We care about hallucinations/regression.
[03:18] Ethan Park: We ran a small eval suite; ROUGE-like and some hallucination checks. Quality delta was within noise for int8 quant with our calibration. We recommended running your task-specific evals (we'll run them next step).
[03:30] Priya Patel: Are there any network/VPC implications if we move to Redwood Private? Like extra hop for control plane?
[03:36] Laura Kim: For Private deployment we can run inference inside your VPC or on-prem. Control plane calls (metrics, rollout) can be proxied or disabled; the data path can be fully customer-hosted so network overhead is minimal, often similar or better than hosted depending on your infra. We'll include a short doc.
[03:52] Maya Singh: Great. Back to numbers: did you look at cost per 1k tokens or any cost proxy? Baseline cost is a big decision factor.
[03:59] Ethan Park: We included rough cost-estimates: on our Dedicated config, raw compute cost-per-1k-tokens was ~30% lower than BaselineCloud for this model under our batching settings. We'll send a cost breakdown in the spreadsheet.
[04:12] Carlos Rivera: Do those cost numbers include network egress or just compute?
[04:15] Ethan Park: Compute only. Network egress depends on region and your cloud discounts. We'll add a line-item for egress estimates.
[04:21] Priya Patel: I noticed in the sheet there was a run labeled "poc-run-3-hotstart" and some numbers looked off, was that a bad run?
[04:27] Ethan Park: Good eye. That run had an autoscaler event on the baseline side mid-run; we flagged it in the notes and excluded it from averages. The raw data's there if you want to inspect.
[04:36] Maya Singh: OK. For next steps, we need a run using our full prompt set (1,200 prompts) at 8k context, and a p99-focused sweep. Can you do that?
[04:45] Ethan Park: Yes, we can schedule a deeper run. It'll take ~48 hours to complete given the queue and will produce per-prompt latency distribution.
[04:51] Laura Kim: Action items and owners coming up, but quick alignment: we'll share the raw spreadsheet + a short writeup of tuning knobs applied. We also propose a short benchmark script so you can run locally against your provider for parity.
[05:02] Carlos Rivera: That would be helpful so we can reproduce. Also we'd like a note on reproducibility and seed configs.
[05:08] Ethan Park: Will include seeds and exact runner commands.
[05:11] Maya Singh: Any security questions from our end that might block a Private eval?
[05:15] Laura Kim: You flagged SSO/SAML and KMS earlier. For Private we support SAML SSO for the control plane, and customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations for key access. We'll send SOC2 docs and an infra diagram.
[05:27] Priya Patel: Great. One last technical: can you enable low-latency routing policy to prefer local region replicas during runs? That might be a fairer comparison to our baseline region setup.
[05:36] Ethan Park: Yes, we can pin region to us-east-1 for the next run if you want. For today's runs most were in us-west-2 but we documented region in each csv.
[05:44] Laura Kim: Okay let's recap next steps.
[05:46] Laura Kim: We'll share the full spreadsheet and a short doc on tuning and kernel choices by tomorrow EOD.
[05:52] Laura Kim: Redwood to run the 8k full-prompt sweep pinned to us-east-1, focused on p99, results in ~48 hours.
[05:59] Ethan Park: We'll also provide the benchmark script and runner config so AtlasAI can reproduce locally.
[06:04] Ethan Park: We'll add network egress estimates and explicit cost line items.
[06:07] Maya Singh: AtlasAI will provide the full 1,200 prompt set and confirm desired SLA targets (p50 < 800ms, p95 < 2s as initial).
[06:18] Carlos Rivera: We'll also check internal procurement for Dedicated access and flag any legal obstacles.
[06:22] Laura Kim: Perfect. Any final questions?
[06:25] Priya Patel: None here, thanks.
[06:27] Maya Singh: Thanks everyone.
[06:29] Laura Kim: Thanks, we'll follow up with notes and schedule the next sync post results.
